A new `/desk-monitor` pane graphs CPU and memory for each Claude session running on this machine.

- `/desk-monitor` lists every running Claude session, this one first, with its state (working, needs input, idle)
- CPU covers the session's process and everything under it (MCP servers, and the shells and commands its tools started, including ones that already ended), drawn as a two-row line graph with the latest value. Memory is the same processes' resident memory as a one-row graph, with the `claude` process alone and the process count below
- All sessions share one scale, so their heights compare. The header gives the totals and the top of each graph, and the graphs cover the last 4 minutes
- It measures every 2 seconds, and only while the pane is drawn. When the pane is closed, folded or behind another tab it stops and drops what it measured
- Click a session's name to go to the herdr tab where it is open
- Linux only: it reads `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` and `/proc/<pid>/stat`
- desk-asana, desk-slack, desk-plan and desk-grant move to 0.71.0 with no changes

## Install

```
/plugin install desk-look --marketplace KyongSik-Yoon/cc-desktop-mod
```

Already installed: `/desk-update` (or `claude plugin update desk-look`), then `/reload-plugins`.
